messages:
Natalie R: Quick design review — updated canary pause modal copy + accessible 'panic' rollback flow. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/XYZ/canary-pause-v3 (see top-right). Screenshot attached. Tom L: looked — main thought: the word 'Pause' reads as temporary but users might think it means 'stop forever'. can we use 'Temporarily pause traffic' as the primary action label? Elaine Chen: +1 to wording. accessibility: when modal opens, focus should land on the primary action and we should announce the state change with an aria-live region. Proposed snippet for SR: ```html
Canary paused — traffic will remain on the configured allocation until you resume or rollback.
``` Jordan P: We also need microcopy for automatic fallback. If the canary degrades, we show a top-banner and auto-fallback after a grace period. Draft: "Automatic fallback: if error rate or latency exceeds threshold for 5 minutes, traffic will revert to the stable deployment. You can disable automatic fallback in advanced settings." Thoughts? Tom L: LGTM. Slight tweak: "Automatic fallback will redirect 100% traffic to the stable deployment if the canary exceeds configured thresholds for 5 minutes." Keep it declarative. Natalie R: UX nit: the pause modal also needs a clear 'Undo' affordance. We should show a toast: "Canary paused — Undo | View rollout history" with keyboard focusable 'Undo' button. Re: keyboard shortcuts — avoid single-letter global shortcuts (they conflict). prefer explicit button. Elaine Chen: Agree on avoiding single-letter shortcuts. Accessibility note: when we auto-fallback, announce via aria-live and push an accessible revision entry into the version history so screen reader users can find what happened. Also update the timeline color for a paused state (suggest #d97706 amber-600) and add a pattern to indicate 'paused by user' vs 'paused by system'. designbot: deploy-preview: Canary pause UI updated in Figma (v3). Preview: https://figma-preview.internal/3456 — includes modal copy edits + toast pattern. :eyes: Jordan P: Copy around rollback vs pause needs a one-line explainer inside the modal: "Pause holds traffic allocation — Rollback returns all traffic to the previous stable version." place under the action buttons in smaller, muted text. Tom L: Accessibility microcopy: change "previous stable version" to the actual label we display in timeline (e.g., "v1.4.2 (stable)") when possible so the toast reads clearly. Natalie R: Final checklist before we ship to QA: 1) modal copy swapped to "Temporarily pause traffic" 2) aria-live assertive message added 3) toast with Undo + View history 4) auto-fallback copy in admin settings 5) contrast check for paused state color 6) timeline entry generation on auto-fallback. I'll update the figma and ping QA. :thumbsup: deploy-bot: preview-deploy: Canary pause changes pushed to staging branch 'canary-pause-v3' at 1728308900. Test link: https://staging.redwood-inference.internal/canary/preview Elaine Chen: small follow-up — ensure keyboard focus order: modal -> primary Pause -> secondary Cancel -> helper link -> close button. Screen reader announcement should include existing allocation (e.g., "Canary currently at 20%"). Tom L: Also suggest adding a short tooltip (?) over the automatic fallback threshold in advanced settings that shows the metric and timeframe. Hover text: "Triggers if error rate > 5% for 5 minutes (configurable)." Natalie R: Awesome. I'll make the copy edits and add the small aria snippet to the handoff notes. tagging @Jordan P for rollout policy copy sign-off. Thanks all.
